title: Core ideas in music
description: The building blocks of music: intervals, scales, keys, chords, rhythm and form.

ideas.title: Intervals
ideas.summary: An interval is the distance between two pitches, counted in semitones and named by its size and quality.

items.q: In music, what is an interval?
items.a: The distance in pitch between two notes

items.q: How many semitones are in an octave?
How many semitones are in a perfect fifth?
Which musical interval spans four semitones, such as C up to E?
items.a: A major third

ideas.title: Scales
ideas.summary: A scale is a ladder of notes within an octave; the major scale follows a fixed pattern of whole and half steps.
links: Keys and the circle of fifths

items.q: What is the pattern of whole and half steps in a major scale?
items.a: Whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half

items.q: Which major scale uses only the white keys of the piano?
items.a: C major

items.q: How many different notes does a major scale have before the octave repeats?
items.a: Seven

items.q: What is a scale with five notes to the octave called?
items.a: A pentatonic scale

ideas.title: Keys and the circle of fifths
ideas.summary: A key is a home note and its scale; moving up a fifth to the next key adds one sharp to the signature.

items.q: In music, what is the tonic of a key?
items.a: The first note of its scale, the home note the music comes to rest on

items.q: What is the relative minor of C major?
items.a: A minor

items.q: How many sharps are in the key signature of G major, and on which note?
items.a: One sharp, F sharp

items.q: On the circle of fifths, what happens to the key signature with each step clockwise?
items.a: It gains one sharp (or loses one flat)

ideas.title: Chords
ideas.summary: A chord is several notes sounded together; a triad stacks two thirds, and the chords on I, IV and V anchor a key.
links: Keys and the circle of fifths

items.q: Which notes make up a C major triad?
items.a: C, E and G

items.q: What makes a triad major rather than minor?
items.a: Its third: a major third above the root, where a minor triad has a minor third

items.q: What is the chord built on the fifth degree of a scale called?
items.a: The dominant

items.q: In the key of C major, which chords are I, IV and V?
items.a: C major, F major and G major

ideas.title: Rhythm and meter
ideas.summary: Meter groups steady beats into measures; a time signature says how many beats and which note gets one.

items.q: In 4/4 time, how many beats are in a measure, and which note gets one beat?
items.a: Four beats; the quarter note gets one

items.q: In written music, what does a dot placed after a note do to its length?
items.a: It adds half the note's value

items.q: In which time signature is a waltz usually written?
In music, what is tempo, and in what unit is it measured?
items.a: The speed of the beat, in beats per minute

ideas.title: Form
ideas.summary: Form is the plan of a piece: which sections repeat, which contrast, and in what order.

items.q: What are the three main sections of sonata form?
items.a: Exposition, development and recapitulation

items.q: Which musical form is described by the letters ABA?
items.a: Ternary form

items.q: In music, what is a rondo?
items.a: A form in which a main theme keeps returning between contrasting sections, as in ABACA

items.q: Which three chords does a standard twelve-bar blues use?
items.a: I, IV and V (the tonic, subdominant and dominant)
